nodes.summary: Let $p(n)$ be the number of partitions of $n$. Over the integers, $\sum_{n \ge 0} p(n)\, x^n$ equals the weighted partition generating function $\sum_{n \ge 0} \sum_{\lambda} \prod_{i} f(i, c_i(\lambda))\, x^n$ with all weights $f(i, c) = 1$, where $\lambda$ runs over the partitions of $n$, $i$ over the distinct parts of $\lambda$, and $c_i(\lambda)$ is the number of times $i$ occurs in $\lambda$.
nodes.title: Partition generating function with unit weights

nodes.summary: Let $p(n)$ be the number of partitions of $n$. Over the integers, $\left(\sum_{n \ge 0} p(n)\, x^n\right) \cdot \sum_{k \in \mathbb{Z}} (-1)^k x^{k(3k-1)/2} = 1$. By the pentagonal number theorem the second factor equals $\prod_{i \ge 1} (1 - x^i)$.
nodes.title: Euler's identity for the partition generating function

nodes.summary: Let $p(n)$ be the number of partitions of $n$. Then $p(1) = 1$: the only partition of $1$ is $1$ itself.
nodes.title: The partition number of one

nodes.summary: Let $p(n)$ be the number of partitions of $n$. Then $p(0) = 1$: the only partition of $0$ is the empty one.
nodes.title: The partition number of zero

nodes.summary: For a natural number $n$, $p(n)$ is the number of partitions of $n$, that is, of ways of writing $n$ as a sum of positive integers, disregarding order.
nodes.title: The partition function

nodes.summary: Let $p(n)$ be the number of partitions of $n$, and for an integer $k$ let $g(k) = k(3k - 1)/2$ be the generalized pentagonal number of $k$. For every natural number $n \ge 1$, $p(n) = \sum_{k} (-1)^{k+1}\, p(n - g(k))$, where the sum runs over the nonzero integers $k$ with $g(k) \le n$.
nodes.title: Euler's pentagonal recurrence for the partition function
